text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Gan Thiam Poh –  4 To ask the Prime Minister (a) what is the total number of people who have downloaded the TraceTogether app; (b) what is the percentage of each gender for those who have downloaded the app; (c) what are the age groups; and (d) whether the Government will consider further incentives and measures to encourage more subscriptions including from those who are not technically savvy or inclined.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Prime Minister whether the download and activation of the TraceTogether app should be made mandatory for everyone in Singapore who possesses a mobile phone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: TraceTogether is basically a contact tracing app which uses your phone's Bluetooth function to detect other phones nearby.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It keeps a record of other TraceTogether users whom you happen to be in close contact with.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It encrypts and stores this data on your own handphone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If, in the unlikely event, you turn out to be positive or diagnosed with COVID-19, this data is then uploaded to MOH, and the contact tracing teams in MOH use this to quickly identify, isolate patients, quarantine people who may be at risk or have been infected by you and can transmit the disease onwards.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The number of downloads, particularly given that it is voluntary, is encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have had repeated discussions both at the technical and policy level with Apple, but we have not yet been able to find a satisfactory solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I believe this will be more inclusive and it will ensure that all of us will be protected.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Notwithstanding the limitations of coverage today, the data from TraceTogether has already been a very helpful additional tool for our contact tracers, especially when it is used in combination with other data sources.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In some cases, it has improved the contact tracing process by automatically generating a preliminary list of close contacts for quarantine, and thereby it reduces the time taken to isolate these contacts and prevents them from spreading the disease more extensively.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Technology is an enabler; it is not a replacement for human judgement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Yesterday, we issued a written response to Mr Murali Pillai who had asked about the confidentiality of the data, and I think it is worth me reiterating that again, that the data is stored only on your own phone in the first instance and accessed by MOH only if the individual tests positive for COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This data is only used for contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: There are safeguards, including encryption, in place to protect this from malicious hackers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If the close contact data is required for contact tracing, only a small group of authorised officers in MOH will have access to it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: All the public sector data protection rules will also apply.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I need to emphasise again that quick and accurate contact tracing is a necessity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In fact, it has become all the more essential now that we are emerging from the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Because if you think about it, if everyone is at home, in fact, the need for contact tracing is minimal.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: But now that we have more people moving about, going to work, there will be more occasions when more people will have more close interactions with each other.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Therefore, the collection and use of this data for contact tracing becomes even more essential.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It will speed up the isolation of close contacts and reduce the risk of them spreading COVID-19 to their loved ones, family members, friends, colleagues and the community at large.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If we can reduce the incidence of clusters by better and faster contact tracing, then we can avoid having to re-introduce restrictive circuit breaker measures in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: So, I hope all members of the public will work with us to achieve this.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister, can I take it that you are answering Question Nos 4 and 5?
